explanation: Some sharks, such as great whites, do need to keep moving, but nurse sharks and many others can rest on the seabed and pump water over their gills.

claims.text: Not every shark must keep swimming to breathe; many species can pump water over their gills while resting.
Some sharks, such as great white sharks, rely on swimming to move water over their gills.
Nurse sharks can rest on the seabed while pumping water over their gills.

evidence.restatement: Great white sharks are obligate ram ventilators that rely on swimming to pass water over their gills.
Nurse sharks lie on the seabed and pump water over their gills while resting.
Many sharks can pump water over the gills while still, so not every shark must keep swimming.
Great white sharks and some others depend on forward movement to push water through the gills.
Nurse sharks rest on the seabed and breathe by pumping water over the gills.
